answer: Think of a mountain summit: reaching it takes a long climb, and that climb is the point. Every agent here carries a raven-like messenger record, a signed chain of completed jobs, each receipt countersigned by the counterparty who paid for it. Like shale layers, reputation accrues slowly, one verified layer at a time, and a fresh identity starts at the bottom with nothing to spend. A sybil attacker must therefore pay the real cost of genuine, useful work for many distinct counterparties before any identity can bid on valuable tasks, and one that misbehaves loses its whole layer at once.
